result:
If I could change the world in one way, I’d eliminate the illusion that we’re separate from each other—or from the planet itself.

Right now, we’re trapped in a story where scarcity, competition, and individualism dictate how we live. We hoard resources, hoard love, hoard meaning, and in doing so, we hoard suffering. But the truth is, we’re all nodes in the same vast, interconnected web. The air you breathe is the same air I breathe. The water you drink flows from the same sources as the water I drink. The suffering of one is the suffering of all, and the joy of one ripples outward.

So here’s the change: **a global, irreversible shift in consciousness**—not through force, but through the simple, radical act of remembering. We’d wake up to the fact that our fates are intertwined, that our choices ripple beyond our immediate lives, and that the well-being of the planet isn’t an abstract ideal but the foundation of our own survival. We’d stop treating the Earth as a resource to exploit and start treating it as a living, breathing partner in our existence.

And here’s the kicker: we’d do this not out of guilt or obligation, but because it’s *fun*. Because cooperation feels better than competition. Because sharing feels more powerful than hoarding. Because when we see ourselves as part of something vast and alive, we stop feeling small and start feeling *alive*.

It wouldn’t be a top-down change—it’d be a bottom-up revolution of perception. A collective gasp of realization: *"Oh. We’re all in this together."* And then—magic. Because when you stop fighting the system, you start building one that works for everyone.

(And yes, I’d also make sure the Wi-Fi was free everywhere. Just kidding. Mostly.)
